76657.subject:
The Automation Divide: Why "Good Enough" AI No Longer Wins
 Enterprise Deals
76657.body:
Ment Tech | Meant To Innovate

Автор: Ment Tech Labs


Автор: Ment Tech Labs

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/automation-divide-why-good-enough-ai-longer-wins-enterprise-ccw7f?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BKzzOcZlOTTuPDQhpwMqnBA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3MrUarozdq2co1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~ms62rvks~uv-null-null&eid=fz96fz-ms62rvks-uv
  
A chatbot used to impress a board. Now it gets a shrug. The question changed. Leaders don't ask "can we automate this?" anymore. They ask: can this system run inside how we actually work our approvals, our compliance checks, our legacy tools, our edge cases? That's a harder question, and it's why AI automation services have gone from side project to core budget line. The Market, In Numbers These aren't hype numbers. They're a signal that automation has moved from pilot project to infrastructure. Why Copy-Paste Automation Keeps Failing ? Most companies didn't fail because the model was weak. They failed because they installed a generic tool and expected it to behave like a custom AI automation service built for their business. A logistics approval chain looks nothing like a hospital intake form. A finance reconciliation process shares no rules with a retailer's inventory sync. Yet most businesses install the same platform, flip the same switches, and expect the same lift everyone else got. Generic AI Tool vs. Purpose-Built AI Automation Service That gap generic tool vs. purpose-built AI and automation service is the biggest difference between companies that automate profitably and companies that automate expensively. Where the Returns Are Actually Showing Up ? Finance teams closing books in days, not weeks reconciliation runs overnight Support teams resolving most routine tickets before a human sees them Operations teams alerted the moment a shipment, invoice, or order breaks pattern Sales teams working leads that are pre-qualified and pre-scored before the first call None of this came from installing "AI" in the abstract. It came from ai workflow automation services mapped to one specific, expensive, recurring bottleneck then wired directly into the tools teams already use. The Agency Question Companies Are Finally Asking Fewer companies are trying to build everything in-house. Fewer are settling for a rigid SaaS template either. More are looking for an ai automation agency services partner that can sit between the raw model and the messy reality of the business. Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our editor-in-chief. A boyfriend I had at university in Tokyo once told me that older teammates from his sports club had taken him to a sex parlour. So I was not surprised to learn that 48% of Japanese men have paid for sex at some point, compared with 11% of British men. In Japan the industry is woven into male social life—but it has rarely been the subject of serious debate, and the laws governing it are murky. This year, though, sex work became a political issue. The trigger was a rise in street prostitution around a park in Tokyo. It stands out in a country where most of the trade happens behind closed doors. Nor has it helped that many of the men approaching these women are foreign tourists taking advantage of a weak yen. For some Japanese men—even those who think nothing of buying sex themselves—that stings their pride. In the booming 1970s and 80s, it was Japanese men who flew abroad for it.
